verdict.headline: Falls faster than gravity allows (17.8 ± 0.9 m/s²).
reasons: Either the footage is sped up, or the object is smaller than assumed (it would need to be 0.55x its assumed size).

tests.name: Constant acceleration
tests.summary: Acceleration holds steady through the fall (+10% half to half).

tests.name: Bounce law
tests.summary: 3 bounce(s) lose energy normally (restitution -1.38-0.80) and hops share one g.

tests.name: Starts from rest
tests.summary: The fall's starting point sits 5.3 ball-widths from where the object was held.

evidence.name: frame timestamps
evidence.detail: High-speed capture: timestamps run at 240 fps of real time. Played back at 30 fps it would look 8x slow.

evidence.name: light flicker
evidence.detail: Lights flicker at 0.27 cycles per frame, which 120 Hz mains produces at 480 fps capture: a hint of 2x slow motion.
